findings.premise: The design covers DEF s2 ac1 (only eligible files admitted from a mixed source; exact revisions, attribution and modifications kept) and ac2 (notices for an exported release carry the required license and attribution records), and builds nothing outside sc3.
findings.evidence: DEF-7e0ae92e8f3d3c3e.json:472-490: ac1 'a source with eligible and unknown-license files … only eligible files are admitted and their exact revisions, attribution and modifications are retained'; ac2 'all included third-party material has the required license and attribution records'. The LLD's ImportReport and the reviewed-policy design (§3.2, §3.4) cover ac1. The deterministic notices and the reconstruction check (§3.5) cover ac2. The ImportReport postcondition rules out publication, catalog writes and IPC/MCP surfaces. [files: .insrc/artifacts/DEF-7e0ae92e8f3d3c3e.json]

findings.premise: The sc3 interface shapes (SourceFile, SourceManifest, ImportReport) match the approved HLD sketch exactly.

findings.premise: Existing git revParse returns short hashes, and shell-helper decodes output as UTF-8 text, so neither can be used to pin a commit or preserve binary bytes.
findings.evidence: helpers.ts:40-42 runs `git rev-parse --short`. shell-helper.ts:89-92 does `stdout += chunk.toString('utf8')` and silently drops bytes past maxBytes (it only sets a stdoutTruncated flag). Both points the design makes are correct. [files: src/daemon/tools/builtins/git/helpers.ts, src/daemon/tools/shell-helper.ts]

findings.premise: candidateContentDigest returns '' unless the coverage path appears exactly once. It also excludes the coverage file's digest and reviewDigest, so eligibility can be bound before the coverage envelope is finalized.
findings.evidence: canonical.ts:96-106: `if (coverage.length !== 1) return ''`, then it deletes releaseId, reviewDigest and coverage[0].digest before hashing. The manifest needs a coverage entry with a path and mediaType, but its bytes and the reviewDigest value do not affect the candidate digest. Source-manifest, notices and lineage file digests do stay in the hash. This confirms the §3.5 assembly order and the 'noncomputable digest → failure' handling. [files: src/design/corpus/canonical.ts]

findings.premise: checkPublication requires exactly one eligibility assessment, bound to the current candidateContentDigest, with passed=true and no issues.
findings.evidence: validate.ts:337-345 requires exactly one assessment per stage. It flags assessment.stale when the digest does not match and assessment.failed when !passed or issues is non-empty. STAGE_ASSESSMENT_SCHEMA (contracts.ts:57-60) requires DIGEST_SCHEMA for candidateContentDigest, so an empty digest cannot even be decoded. That justifies the design's 'do not construct a StageAssessment with an empty digest'. [files: src/design/corpus/validate.ts, src/design/corpus/contracts.ts]

findings.premise: S002 reuses S001's 'portable path rules and NFC/case collision comparisons' and UTC ISO validation (for retrievedAt) as existing helpers.
findings.evidence: validate.ts:16 exports `isPortablePath`, but `pathCollisionKey` (validate.ts:20, `path.normalize('NFC').toLowerCase()`) and `utcDate` (validate.ts:21) are module-private `const`/`function` with no export. index.ts re-exports only exported symbols. To reuse them as written, S002 must either add exports to S001's validate.ts, which touches the S001 surface the design says it leaves unchanged, or duplicate the logic, which risks drifting from S001's collision and timestamp rules. [files: src/design/corpus/validate.ts, src/design/corpus/index.ts]
findings.action: State in §3.1 whether S002 adds `pathCollisionKey`/`utcDate` exports to src/design/corpus/validate.ts (and list that as a change site) or duplicates them with a parity test against S001 behaviour.

findings.premise: The ValidationIssue codes the error paths use (provenance.incomplete, reference.missing, digest.mismatch, path.invalid, inventory.invalid, limit.exceeded) already exist in S001, so no S001 schema change is needed.
findings.evidence: contracts.ts:53-55 ISSUE_CODES includes all six codes. [files: src/design/corpus/contracts.ts]

findings.evidence: canonical.ts:5 `CORPUS_LIMITS = { recordBytes: 1 MiB, packageBytes: 64 MiB, files: 10_000, depth: 64 }`, exported. [files: src/design/corpus/canonical.ts]

findings.premise: New sources/* modules can be added without changing S001's public barrel, and the Git reader stays out of the pure src/design/corpus/index.ts.
findings.evidence: index.ts re-exports only contracts/canonical/validate. module-isolation.test.ts:11-56 compiles the corpus and imports out/design/corpus/index.js with fs/net/child_process forbidden, so a pure-boundary smoke test already has a template to extend. The design names a separate entry for git-reader.ts. [files: src/design/corpus/index.ts, src/design/corpus/__tests__/module-isolation.test.ts]
findings.action: None. Make sure the pure-boundary test also covers the new pure sources entry (eligibility/notices), not just index.js.

findings.premise: Lineage stored as a separate file (sources/lineage.json) listed in manifest.files is covered by candidate hashing, and S001's release validation accepts it without schema change.
findings.evidence: canonical.ts:96-105 hashes every manifest.files entry (path, digest, mediaType) except the coverage digest. validate.ts:193-207 accepts any declared regular file and treats files that are neither records nor sourceManifest/notices/coverage as contentPaths. An extra lineage file therefore validates and is bound by the digest. The manifest has no lineagePath field, so S002 has to find it at the fixed path, as the design states. [files: src/design/corpus/canonical.ts, src/design/corpus/validate.ts]

findings.premise: Package paths derived from upstream repository paths can be validated with S001's portable path rule.
findings.evidence: isPortablePath (validate.ts:16-19) rejects '\\', '%', ':' and control characters. Real upstream paths can contain '%' or ':', and the design applies the S001 rule to SourceFile.path. This rejects them as path.invalid rather than marking them unresolved, which fits 'unsafe paths → abort request'. However, one such path aborts the whole mixed import. I could not tell from the design whether that is intended (§5 makes the unsafe-path case request-level) or whether such files should be reported per file. [files: src/design/corpus/validate.ts]
findings.action: Clarify whether a non-portable upstream path fails the whole request or only that file.

findings.premise: S002 does no catalog/package installation (S004), coverage (S003/sc4) or publication (S005). It produces only the 'eligibility' stage and does not change sc1/sc2.
findings.evidence: HLD:274-282 sc3 is ownedByStory s2. The LLD keeps staging in memory ('durable catalog/package installation remains S004'), emits stage='eligibility' only, and says 'No changes to S001 public schema'. S001's LLD (LLD-…-s1.json:414) defines a dependency-inverted assessment input for downstream eligibility, which this matches. The only boundary pressure is the unexported-helper issue raised under new-versus-reuse. [files: .insrc/artifacts/HLD-7e0ae92e8f3d3c3e.json, .insrc/artifacts/LLD-7e0ae92e8f3d3c3e-s1.json]

findings.premise: Each failure is detectable and its handling is stated consistently. In particular, a digest mismatch is handled the same way across the error-path list.
findings.evidence: §5 case 1 says 'mismatched evidence digests' → mark the path unresolved (per file, other files still admitted). §5 case 3 says 'mismatched source bytes' → 'Request-level ValidationResult failure … no partial admitted result'. §3.3 also fails the whole request on 'digest mismatch'. With ac1 (DEF:475-477) requiring a mixed source to still admit eligible files, an implementer cannot tell whether a stale reviewed-profile digest for one file should abort the whole import or leave that file unresolved. The two choices give different ImportReports and different test expectations. [files: .insrc/artifacts/DEF-7e0ae92e8f3d3c3e.json]
findings.action: Define one rule: for example, a stale profile digest for one file → that file unresolved, while a Git object or framing integrity failure → request-level failure. Align §3.3, §5 and the mixed-eligibility and reader-safety tests with it.

new-versus-reuse.1.note: Specified S002-local collision/timestamp primitives and parity matrix against S001 public behavior; only isPortablePath is reused as an export. No S001 surface change.

error-paths.1.note: Aligned acquisition and eligibility: stale reviewed file/evidence digests yield per-file unresolved outcomes propagated to dependents; Git acquisition-integrity failures abort the request. Updated data model, error paths and test subjects.

data-compatibility.2.note: Made strict v1 selected-path grammar explicit: any requested non-portable path aborts before I/O, while unselected paths have no effect. Added edge case and reader-safety test requirement.

summary.prose: Admit reviewed material from exact local source revisions and preserve its attribution through release packaging. S002 adds file-level eligibility, traceable source-to-output bindings and reproducible notices, with a separate bounded Git reader. It consumes S001 identities and leaves editorial coverage and publication to later stories.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose immutable release packages with a daemon-owned catalog and rebuildable retrieval indexes. Shared contracts below are proposed additions, not existing APIs. Corpus data is global public knowledge, independent of registered source repositories; DI2 owns project-private guideline storage and DI3 owns authoring workflows.

ownedContracts.name: File-level source eligibility and attribution
ownedContracts.purpose: Keep file licenses, exact upstream revisions and notices with every derived asset; repository license alone never admits content.

consumedContracts.name: Corpus record and pinned evidence identity
consumedContracts.purpose: Common immutable record, provenance and release identity across all stories and DI2/DI3.

consumedContracts.name: Release manifest and publication gate
consumedContracts.purpose: s1 establishes envelopes and gates used by import, curation, query and maintenance; s2 implements ingestion. Publication requires nonempty problem/tradeoffs, checks with explicit limits (or an explicit no-measurable-check rationale), and domainPayload.color/layout/style for corresponding color/layout/style records. Semantic roles and pairings must reference declared roles; examples and misuse examples must be present for every declared platform. Domain validation rejects an empty placeholder.

boundary.internal: Own source adapters, local staging extraction, allowlist policy implementation and reproducible notices. Adapter specifics stay private; no unreviewed source contents enter published assets.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own canonical schema, version/hash specification, publication validation interfaces and fixtures. This is the nearest ancestor for all shared identity/release contracts; storage and curator UI are not implied.

Own authored seed records, declarative specimens and reviewed coverage across ten domains and three UI types. A release names its maintainer/reviewer; unknown source sufficiency cannot be counted as coverage.

Own daemon package reader, catalog read adapter, deterministic filtering/ranking, local embedding cache, cursor implementation and thin MCP read tools. Keep ranking weights and cache format private and versioned. Basic validated bundled-package installation is included so retrieval is independently testable. Includes the single-sourced config-catalog entry, typed config exposure, settings/reconciliation verification and catalog contract-test update. Owns vscode-plugin/package.json setting mirror and verification of the unchanged catalog-driven JetBrains SettingsView.kt, validated by manifest/catalog parity and settings render/round-trip checks. Sole owner of catalog file layout, serialized atomic commit, receipts and recovery via sc7. Basic installation and maintenance use exactly this writer.

Own update staging, atomic publish/default switch, withdrawal overlays, recovery, release diffs and cross-release regression evaluation. Consume existing reader contracts; never change DI2 guideline state. Uses sc7 for all catalog/default/availability changes; owns upstream update policy and diff orchestration only, not a second writer or recovery implementation.

nonFunctional.performance: For a representative 1,000-record seed fixture, measure warm query p95 <=500 ms excluding local embedding inference; report embedding latency separately. This is a target, not a benchmark claim. If exceeded, optimize indexing without dropping eligible candidates; complete-result quality takes precedence. Cold index building is resumable and serial.
nonFunctional.security: Only eligible reviewed material is distributed. Validate all package paths and sizes, reject executable specimen content and remote includes; escape rendering. No arbitrary URL fetching at query time. Unknown hard constraints return gaps. Do not mix project-private data into the public corpus or embedding index.
nonFunctional.observability: Log release ID, query mode, eligible/matched counts, filter/gap reasons, index fingerprint and validation codes; avoid storing user query/brief text by default. Expose install/index health and explicit degraded retrieval, rather than silent fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Immutable package bytes plus atomic catalog and append-only availability events. Rebuild derived indexes on checksum/model mismatch. Inject crashes between each publication boundary; old release remains readable or a newly complete release becomes visible, never partial content. Retain pinned references across rollback; policy withdrawal returns tombstones.

api.name: SourceManifest

returns.meaning: Closed, versioned sc3 source metadata for material actually included in a candidate; review decisions and exact upstream identity remain inspectable.

errors.condition: Invalid structure, duplicate source identity, unpinned revision, unresolved evidence or inconsistent eligibility.

preconditions: Decode unknown inputs from detached canonical JSON; never trust TypeScript types or an eligible label as proof.
Review descriptors and policy are maintainer-controlled local inputs; incoming repository content cannot set or amend policy.
postconditions: Exact sc3 fields retained without coercion, stripping, inferred authorship or dropped modifications.
Published source metadata contains only included eligible material and its complete required evidence closure; rejected inputs stay in the staging report. [[c2]]

api.name: ImportReport
api.signature: interface ImportReport { admitted: string[]; excluded: { path: string; reason: string }[]; unresolved: string[]; }

returns.meaning: Deterministically sorted per-file outcomes for one repository/revision import. Entries use upstream relative paths within that request; reports for multiple sources remain separate.

errors.condition: Request-wide safety/integrity failure prevents returning any admitted bytes.

preconditions: A request binds one allowlisted repository URL, an existing local repository and one full commit object ID.
Only exact listed paths may be acquired; no mutable branch/tag expansion, recursive checkout, network or subprocess hooks.
postconditions: Eligible files alone produce staged bytes; unknown decisions appear in unresolved and ship no bytes; excluded entries carry reasons.
No publication, catalog mutation, project-guideline change or user-facing IPC/MCP surface is introduced. [[c2]]

api.name: StageAssessment
api.signature: interface StageAssessment { stage: 'eligibility' | 'coverage'; candidateContentDigest: string; passed: boolean; issues: ValidationIssue[]; }

returns.meaning: Consumed S001 envelope. S002 produces only stage='eligibility' after checking complete candidate lineage and notices; downstream supplies coverage.

errors.condition: Unknown policy, missing lineage, omitted obligations, changed source/output bytes or noncomputable identity prevents a passing assessment.

preconditions: Candidate inventory is snapshotted and checked with sc1/sc2 helpers; candidate digest must be nonempty.
Full editorial coverage review is not required to compute eligibility: verify structural/source/notice/record invariants without requiring the future coverage envelope's finalized bytes.
postconditions: The assessment binds corrected candidateContentDigest and all source/notices role metadata.
Failure with noncomputable digest returns ValidationResult failure rather than constructing a StageAssessment with an invalid empty digest. No changes to S001 public schema. [[c3]]

dataModelChanges.entity: sc3 closed schemas and source identities
dataModelChanges.details: Proposed src/design/corpus/sources/contracts.ts defines exact sc3 runtime TypeBox schemas with Static-derived types, reusing S001 digest/issue primitives. SourceFile.sourceId uniquely names one repositoryUrl/revision/path tuple within a release; use a stable namespaced lowercase identifier derived from SHA-256 of canonical tuple, and reject duplicate IDs or inconsistent tuples. revision is a full Git commit OID (40 or 64 lowercase hex), digest is raw blob SHA-256; retrievedAt is validated UTC ISO supplied by the caller, not wall-clock-generated. path and all distributed evidence refs use S001 portable path rules and NFC/case collision comparisons. Reference-only source links are not SourceFile admission records. GuidanceRecord.provenance.sourceRefs resolves exactly to sourceId entries for imported/derived material; no URL guessing or source-ID aliases. [[c2]] [[c3]] Reuse only the exported isPortablePath helper. pathCollisionKey and utcDate are private in S001; S002 will implement small local equivalents in sources/validation-primitives.ts, with behavioral parity tests against S001 public validators. Collision equivalence is NFC normalization followed by toLowerCase; timestamps accept only real UTC calendar instants whose ISO round-trip exactly matches YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss[.sss]Z. No exports or code changes in S001 validate.ts/index.ts are proposed. The parity matrix includes NFC-equivalent paths, case collisions, C0/C1 characters, leap days, impossible dates, fractional-second precision and offsets. [[c3]]

Proposed sources/policy.ts carries a closed versioned policy of exact canonical repository URLs plus explicitly reviewed file profiles. A profile binds repository, full commit, exact paths, SHA-256 bytes, reviewedBy, eligibilityReason, resolved license identifiers, license/notice evidence paths and their digests, attribution, required modification notices and relevant redistribution conditions. The initial license categories follow PRD preferences MIT, Apache-2.0 and CC0-1.0, but an ID alone never admits a file; the reviewed profile must resolve actual file terms and exceptions. Open-font categories require an explicit reviewed category/profile with reserved-name/other conditions recorded before admission; no generic font allowance. Unknown license, unsupported expression, conflicting IDs/terms or a missing file-specific review yields unresolved. Explicit disallowed terms yield excluded. Multiple IDs do not mean automatically choosing the most permissive; unresolved OR/AND/exception expressions require a maintainer to supply an unambiguous reviewed profile under a versioned policy. Repository code licenses never cover external sites/assets automatically. Checks implement recorded decisions, not automated legal interpretation. No network lookup, model inference or source-controlled policy modification. [[c1]] [[c4]]

Proposed sources/git-reader.ts is a separate I/O entry, never re-exported by the pure src/design/corpus/index.ts. Acquire only from a caller-supplied existing local Git repository; no clone/fetch or worktree reads. Verify full supplied OID identifies a commit, enumerate exact literal selected tree paths, reject symlink/submodule/non-blob entries, then read blobs at that commit. Dirty worktree changes cannot affect bytes. Use shell:false argv, literal path matching, fixed read-only Git subcommands, disable replacement objects and lazy fetching, exclude inherited Git command/config overrides, and bound stdout/stderr/time and abort children; never silently truncate. Existing shell-helper emits decoded text and git revParse emits short hashes, so do not use them for byte preservation/pinning. The internal injectable reader returns copied Uint8Array blobs plus verified object kind/path/commit for pure tests. Enforce <=10,000 selected files and <=64 MiB aggregate staged bytes using S001 safety limits, <=30 seconds per child, and fail the request without admitted bytes on truncation, timeout, absent OID/path, Git object/framing integrity failure, malformed output or cancellation. Git LFS pointers and submodules stay unresolved unless a future approved adapter supplies verified content; never follow them or trigger filters. Staging is an in-memory result; durable catalog/package installation remains S004. [[c3]] [[c5]] Distinguish verified acquisition from profile eligibility: successfully acquired blob bytes that differ from a reviewed profile digest make only that file unresolved; no bytes from it or from dependents requiring its evidence are admitted. An invalid Git object/type/framing or inconsistent acquisition result aborts the request. Validate explicitly requested upstream paths before I/O: any non-portable requested path (including percent or colon) aborts the entire request with path.invalid, rather than silently skipping it. Unselected upstream paths are not enumerated for admission and cannot invalidate the request. This strict v1 request grammar is separate from mixed license eligibility. [[c2]]

Proposed sources/eligibility.ts accepts detached reviewed descriptors, policy, acquired blobs and the candidate's records/file inventory. Separate staging decisions from candidate assessment: evaluate every exact requested file against the profile and evidence digests, return mixed ImportReport plus only admitted copied bytes. A rejected/unresolved source cannot be referenced by included records or outputs. Internal output bindings map each included third-party package path and digest to nonempty sourceIds, transformation identifier and explicit modification notes; imported byte copies require equality to upstream digest, derived bytes require their own digest and recorded transformations/reviewer rather than a false equality assertion. Bindings are serialized within a separate deterministic lineage JSON file listed in the manifest, so candidate hashing covers them without changing sc3; its fixed package path is sources/lineage.json and schema version 1. Records' sourceRefs and modificationNotes must agree with bindings; shared specimens union all contributing sources. Original and independently inferred records identify author/rationale and cannot silently wrap unbound third-party assets. A missing binding for any non-original specimen/output fails provenance.incomplete. Require explicit original-output declarations with author and rationale in the same lineage file for package content with no upstream sources; metadata/evidence files use their own explicit categories. Closure includes license and notice evidence, their raw digests and attribution; no dependency is admitted on repository reputation. [[c2]] [[c3]] A stale file or license/notice evidence profile digest is a per-file unresolved eligibility result, propagated to every requested file depending on that evidence; other independently eligible files still appear in admitted. No stale bytes are distributed. Acquisition-integrity failures remain request-level as specified by the reader. [[c2]]

Proposed sources/notices.ts emits deterministic UTF-8 NOTICE text plus unchanged license/notice evidence bytes under portable package paths. Sort by sourceId/path using code-unit order, deduplicate identical evidence bytes by digest while retaining every source association, preserve original text exactly in evidence files, and include exact repository/commit/path/digest, license IDs, attribution, modifications and reviewed provenance. No current time, absolute machine paths or locale-dependent sorting. Binary assets are not interpreted as text; evidence text decoding is strict and bounded. Before returning passing eligibility, independently reconstruct expected source manifest/lineage/notices from included bindings and reviewed profiles and compare exact candidate metadata bytes and evidence inventory: a formatter invocation is not proof that all obligations were included. Missing evidence, modified notice bytes, omitted contributor, stale profile or source-reference mismatch blocks. Required notice/license refs must resolve to included immutable evidence files, not remote URLs or local absolute paths. SourceManifest contains admitted source/evidence entries; staging rejects stay in ImportReport outside distributed bytes. Candidate assembly order: admitted source/output bytes → source manifest/lineage/notices → manifest with coverage path/mediaType placeholder → nonempty candidate digest → eligibility assessment → S003 coverage envelope → final release digest → S001 complete preflight. This avoids requiring a finalized coverage envelope to compute eligibility, and no SourceManifest or lineage file embeds candidate/final release digests. [[c2]] [[c3]]

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Exact SourceFile/SourceManifest/ImportReport shapes, reviewed eligibility, pinned local extraction and deterministic obligation closure. Internal profiles, bindings and adapter seams remain S002-owned. [[c2]]
Resolve sourceRefs and preserve original/derived/imported/inferred labels, source identity and modification lineage; do not change record schemas. [[c3]]
Use raw byte and corrected manifest hashes, portable inventory validation and candidate-bound eligibility assessments. No publication/catalog write; no coverage algorithm. [[c3]]

errorCases.scenario: Unknown, absent or conflicting file terms
errorCases.detection: Resolve the exact file profile and policy category; detect absent review, unsupported expressions, and SHA-256 disagreement between successfully acquired bytes and reviewed file or evidence profiles.
errorCases.response: Mark the affected path and every requested dependent of stale evidence unresolved; admit no affected bytes. Other independently eligible files may be admitted. Candidate references to unresolved material fail provenance.incomplete.
errorCases.userImpact: Maintainer must supply a reviewed file-specific decision.

errorCases.scenario: Explicitly excluded source or non-allowlisted repository
errorCases.detection: Compare exact repository URL and selected path/profile against versioned policy.
errorCases.response: Exclude with stable reason; no bytes admitted.
errorCases.userImpact: A blocked file cannot enter a distributed candidate.

errorCases.scenario: Missing pinned revision/path or Git acquisition-integrity failure
errorCases.detection: Verify full commit type, exact tree/blob identity and complete binary framing; distinguish an invalid/inconsistent acquisition result from valid bytes that merely differ from a stale reviewed profile.
errorCases.response: Request-level ValidationResult failure with digest.mismatch, inventory.invalid or reference.missing; no admitted result. A reviewed-profile digest mismatch after successful acquisition instead follows the per-file unresolved rule.
errorCases.userImpact: Re-pin and review the intended revision.

errorCases.scenario: Unsafe paths, duplicate IDs, symlinks/submodules or limit excess
errorCases.detection: Apply portable path and NFC/case collision checks, unique sourceId tuple checks, tree modes and incremental byte/time bounds.
errorCases.response: path.invalid, inventory.invalid, reference.missing or limit.exceeded; abort request and release subprocess/resources. Any explicitly requested non-portable upstream path, including percent/colon, aborts the entire request before I/O; unselected paths have no effect.
errorCases.userImpact: Correct the input; no traversal, lazy fetch, filters or truncated output.

errorCases.detection: Reconstruct exact expected metadata/evidence closure from admitted profiles and output bindings; compare candidate inventory hashes and bytes.
errorCases.response: provenance.incomplete, reference.missing or digest.mismatch; passing eligibility is withheld.

errorCases.scenario: Unbound third-party specimen or inconsistent record sourceRefs
errorCases.detection: Join each package output to source bindings or explicit original declarations; compare record provenance source IDs and modification notes.
errorCases.response: provenance.incomplete; output cannot be admitted based on an original record label alone.
errorCases.userImpact: Record the actual contributors and transformations.

errorCases.detection: Count coverage-path membership and call corrected candidateContentDigest; empty digest is not a valid assessment binding.
errorCases.response: ValidationResult failure; do not emit a malformed StageAssessment. Preserve sc1/sc2 diagnostics.

errorCases.scenario: Git unavailable, timeout, cancellation or malformed binary stream
errorCases.detection: Observe subprocess exit/signal, abort state, bounded stderr/stdout and object framing.
errorCases.response: Request-level failure with no admitted bytes; release buffers and child handles; sanitized error includes stable category, not raw source content.
errorCases.userImpact: Retry after fixing local checkout or environment.

edgeCases.input: Mixed eligible and unknown-license files at one pinned commit
edgeCases.expected: A successful staging report admits only eligible files with complete evidence; unresolved bytes are absent. A candidate that references unresolved sources still fails.

edgeCases.input: Two source files share an identical license text
edgeCases.expected: Deduplicate stored evidence by digest while retaining both source associations and all attributions.

edgeCases.input: Dirty worktree or branch moves after the request
edgeCases.expected: Read only the verified full commit object; pinned bytes and notices stay unchanged.

edgeCases.input: Original guidance with no upstream sources
edgeCases.expected: Explicit original-output declarations and record author/rationale remain required; do not fabricate third-party attribution.
Bindings contain the union of sourceIds and modification records; notices cover all contributors.

edgeCases.input: Font or dual-license file lacks an explicit policy decision
edgeCases.expected: Unresolved and absent from admitted bytes; no permissive license guessed.
The manifest already declares coverage path/mediaType; eligibility binds non-cyclic content and does not require S003 editorial completion.

edgeCases.input: One successfully read file differs from its reviewed digest
edgeCases.expected: That file and dependents of its stale evidence are unresolved; other independently eligible files are admitted. Git object/framing integrity failure instead aborts the whole request.

edgeCases.input: An explicitly requested upstream path contains percent or colon
edgeCases.expected: Reject the entire request as path.invalid before I/O under the strict v1 grammar. The same path elsewhere in the unselected repository has no effect.

invariantsToPreserve.text: sc3 public interfaces and adjacent story boundaries stay as approved; no catalog writer or guidelines workflow here.
Candidate hash covers all non-cyclic manifest metadata; eligibility output is a trusted internal result, not caller authorization.
Pure sc1/sc2 barrel imports remain free of file/network/provider side effects; Git reader is a separate entry point.
Accuracy and retained provenance take precedence over automatic guesses; no direct cloud calls or provider use.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test + node:assert/strict via tsx, matching direct reads of existing corpus tests after empty graph test/convention probes.

testLevels.purpose: Prove sc3 schema and file-level reviewed policy without Git or real third-party content.
subjects: source-schema: exact sc3 round-trip, strict unknown fields, unique IDs, full revisions and portable evidence refs

mixed-eligibility: eligible/unknown/conflicting/excluded files, expression and font-profile handling, no label-only admission; stale file/evidence profiles remain per-file unresolved and propagate to dependents
lineage-closure: multi-source derived outputs, original declarations, record sourceRefs and modifications, no unbound specimens
validation-parity: local collision/timestamp primitives match S001 public-validator behavior on the shared adversarial matrix without exporting private S001 helpers
fixturesNeeded: Independently authored text/binary files with synthetic reviewed policy descriptors; labels represent test decisions, not legal assertions.

testLevels.purpose: Prove complete deterministic notices and candidate binding.
subjects: notice-closure: every included source and obligation retained, byte-exact evidence, deterministic ordering and shared evidence deduplication
eligibility-binding: swapped source/notices roles, changed attribution/output/evidence bytes and stale profiles invalidate assessments
acyclic-staging: coverage placeholder enables eligibility before coverage finalization; zero/duplicate coverage membership yields failure rather than an empty StageAssessment
fixturesNeeded: Complete synthetic source/lineage/NOTICE manifest plus S001 record and package fixtures; independently specified expected notice bytes.

testLevels.purpose: Prove pinned extraction with temporary local repositories and a controlled process seam.
subjects: pinned-reader: exact commit bytes despite dirty worktree/branch movement; binary round-trip and missing revision/path

reader-safety: symlink/submodule/LFS rejection, unsafe paths, collisions, byte/count/time limits, cancellation and subprocess failure with no admitted bytes; acquisition-integrity failures abort the request, and any selected non-portable path fails before I/O while unselected paths do not
candidate-roundtrip: mixed source staging through source manifest/notices/lineage and S001 preflight, with complete exported inventory
fixturesNeeded: Temporary repositories under OS temp dirs, fixed authored commit contents and explicit input timestamps; injected failures for bounded process behavior.

testLevels.purpose: Preserve runtime boundaries and strict compilation.
subjects: pure-boundary: sc1/sc2 import and pure eligibility/notices run with I/O forbidden; Git adapter imported separately
strict-build: npm run build and all corpus tests under supported Node
fixturesNeeded: Fresh private compilation output; no daemon store, live network, installed source assets or provider.

alternativesConsidered.name: Pure eligibility core with separate pinned Git reader
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep policy and notices deterministic; isolate local Git access behind a binary reader.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Implement sc3 schemas and pure file-level eligibility/notice composition in a sources module. A separate local Git adapter reads exact commit blobs into bounded memory with an injectable byte-reader; both consume sc1/sc2 identities. Human-reviewed source descriptors select exact files and obligations, never infer eligibility from repository labels.
pros: Directly test mixed-license and notice closure with no live dependencies.
Preserves pure sc1/sc2 barrel and exact upstream bytes.
Local adapter is separately testable with temporary repositories.
cons: Requires a binary-safe Git reader because existing runShell exposes text.
Maintainers supply reviewed exact-file descriptors rather than automatic license guesses.

alternativesConsidered.name: Single filesystem importer with policy and notice generation
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Combine pinned extraction, eligibility and output generation into one import service.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Implement sc3 in a local staging service which reads exact commit blobs, performs reviewed file-level policy checks and emits notices. Keep the same sc1/sc2 shapes and no catalog writes, with integration tests around temporary repositories.
cons: Harder to isolate policy determinism and malformed-input behavior.
Combines filesystem/subprocess concerns with reusable publication assessment logic.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets outputs but entangles pure eligibility with I/O and weakens fault isolation.
